calls.head: Don’t buy Vejmelka’s record against the Sabres
calls.body: Since 2023-24, Vejmelka has been a wall against the Sabres, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Sabres finally get to him.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Mammoth beat the Sabres
paras: Tage Thompson got the scoring started for the Sabres on the power play midway through the first, but they didn’t score again. Kailer Yamamoto made it 1-1 for Utah a little over two minutes later, in his first game of the season. Nick Schmaltz and Anders Lee scored just over two minutes apart late in the second to put the Mammoth up 3-1. MacKenzie Weegar and Peyton Krebs squared off later in the period. John Marino stretched the lead to 4-1 on the power play early in the third.
The Mammoth drove the play, outshooting the Sabres 30-24, and the scoreboard caught up. Karel Vejmelka made 23 saves for the Mammoth, and Colten Ellis stopped 26 of 30 at the other end.
Vejmelka picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Mammoth improved to 4-2-0 and climbed into first in the Central, while the Sabres dropped to 2-3-0, slipping to seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: Clayton Keller extended his point streak against Buffalo to six games.
The Mammoth have beaten the Sabres five straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
John Marino scored his first goal of the season, his first since Jan 15 (37 games played since).
One of the preview’s two calls held.
